title: Kajabi Alternatives: Top Picks Compared (2026 Guide)
summary: Kajabi alternatives vary in entry price, transaction fees, and caps on products or contacts. Find which platform suits your budget and feature needs.
body_markdown:
## Activepieces


Activepieces connects your course platform to your CRM, email and chat without replacing any of them, using an MIT-licensed core and 750 integrations counted in its public GitHub monorepo.


That matters because the platform you land on, whether Systeme.io, Thinkific or Teachable, will probably do less out of the box than Kajabi did.


The gap Kajabi leaves is usually the glue: the small automatic actions that used to happen without you thinking about it.


Think about what Kajabi did quietly in the background. A student buys, gets tagged, lands on the right email list, and receives a welcome message.


When you move to a cheaper tool, those steps don't vanish from your business. They just stop happening unless someone does them by hand.


Doing nothing about that costs you hours every week, plus the occasional customer who paid and heard nothing back.


### Rebuilding Kajabi's background steps


To rebuild those steps, you set them up in Activepieces as workflows, which the free plan covers at $0 with 1,000 credits a month. You pick a trigger, such as a new enrollment.


You then tell it what should follow: add the person to your CRM (the customer database), subscribe them to an email list, post in a chat channel so you know someone joined.


You build it by connecting blocks in a visual editor, so you don't need to write code to get started.


In the picture below, your course platform on the left feeds Activepieces in the middle, which hands the right information to the CRM, email and chat tools on the right.


Take from it that the course platform is one connection among many, roughly 60% of the integrations being community-contributed, so it stays interchangeable.


If you switch from Teachable to Thinkific next year, you reconnect one side of the diagram and leave the rest alone.


*(illustration)*


The tagging, the welcome email and the Slack alert can each be their own small flow, because the Activepieces pricing page lists "unlimited flows" on every tier from Free through Ultimate, and a run costs 1 credit however many steps it has.


Zapier's pricing page bills a task per action and Make's a credit per module, so on both, the tidy version of this setup costs more every time it runs.


### Cloud or self-hosted


You can run Activepieces on their hosted cloud, or host it yourself on a server you control. Cloud is the quicker start, and its free plan costs $0.


Self-hosting runs the free Community Edition under the MIT licence, and suits you if you want your data on your own machine and are comfortable maintaining a server, or paying someone who is.


### What Activepieces doesn't do


One limit is worth stating plainly: **Activepieces sells no courses and hosts none** . It has no checkout, no lesson pages, no student logins.


You still need a platform for that, and Activepieces connects to it through its 750 integrations, which is why the choice in the earlier sections comes first.


Once that choice is made, the automation layer is what lets you keep the Kajabi behavior you liked without paying for the Kajabi bundle.
